Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-05
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood CSM), Ethan Morales (BrightPath CTO), Lena Park (BrightPath SRE), Marcus Nguyen (BrightPath Data Platform), Rita Osei (BrightPath Security)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick check-in on POC onboarding velocity, status of VPC peering and credential handoff, initial benchmark anomalies (latency spikes under burst), and next steps for canary traffic. Security questions around KMS/HSM and audit logs noted.

Topics: onboarding checklist, access gating, staging vs prod parity, KV cache warmup, quantization profile impact, SOC2/SSO, canary timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining on short notice, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick off— how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Ethan: doing good, thanks. We got a busy week, wanted to make sure we keep the momentum on the pilot.
[00:12] Priya: hey all, priya here — i'll be focused on the bench runs and the kv cache stuff. quick note: we tried the 8k sequence test overnight and saw a couple of spikes.
[00:22] Lena: yes saw that, from our side the staging cluster had a tail latency outlier at 1.6s per token for a short period, unexpected.
[00:30] Marcus: hi, quick context — we're proxying traffic through our envoy mesh in staging, and also replaying from the traffic capture; might be something with request shaping.
[00:38] Jordan: ok good, let's capture that. Carlos — any updates on creds handoff?
[00:42] Carlos: we sent the service account key last night but looks like the allowlist still needs the BrightPath egress range added, they pinged support for that.
[00:49] Rita: yeah, security flagged that. also we have questions on KMS: are keys customer-managed, and do you support HSM-backed keys?
[00:57] Priya: short answer: we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations, HSM depends on the private deployment — for hosted we can integrate with customer KMS in most clouds; i'll follow up with exact certs and requirements.
[01:10] Ethan: can you send the SOC2 level and audit log retention docs? our compliance team expects details.
[01:15] Jordan: yes that's in the security packet — i'll share the doc link after the call.
[01:18] Jordan: okay let me run down agenda: 1) access & creds status 2) bench anomalies and root cause suspects 3) sequencing and kv cache warmup tips 4) next steps and canary timeline.
[01:30] Marcus: sounds good. on access: we have the service principal but not the VPC peering CIDR confirmed, so staging traffic is still via a proxy hop.
[01:40] Jordan: that could explain the extra hop latency. can you confirm the CIDR?
[01:44] Marcus: i'll confirm — right now it's 10.12.0.0/16 for staging egress, but we need to make sure there's no overlap with your infra.
[01:52] Priya: if there's overlap, routing will SNAT and add latency; prefer direct peering, that eliminates NAT.
[01:58] Lena: ok we'll prioritize that.
[02:02] Jordan: on the bench anomalies — priya, quick summary of what you saw?
[02:06] Priya: ran three profiles: steady QPS 50, burst 1k concurrent short requests, and long-context 8k. steady was fine, burst had token-per-second burst spikes, and the 8k run showed memory-pressure-induced kv cache evictions at step ~820 which led to regen of cache and a spike.
[02:22] Marcus: evictions? is that a model memory footprint issue or orchestration?
[02:26] Priya: looks like it's model state + sequence length. the runtime tries to keep a kv cache but our staging scheduler set a lower memory headroom. increasing headroom or adjusting batch sizing fixes it.
[02:36] Jordan: note — that's consistent with early onboarding runs we saw with other customers; common fix is tuning the batch size and reserving kv cache memory.
[02:44] Lena: what about quantization profile — we used 4-bit in staging, could that cause token-time variance?
[02:50] Priya: potentially, 4-bit quant helps cost but alters kernel paths; some kernels are slower for longer sequences on certain GPUs. i'll run a direct compare 4-bit vs 8-bit and attach perf deltas.
[03:02] Rita: and for encryption, logs — where do the audit logs land and do you rotate them?
[03:07] Carlos: logs can be forwarded to their S3 or our customer logging sink; retention configurable — will include rotation policy in the doc.
[03:14] Ethan: our big blocker is production parity — staging currently has the envoy hop and different quant profile, so hard to sign off on canary.
[03:22] Jordan: agreed — let's prioritize parity: 1) VPC peering, 2) same quant profile as prod (we can mirror), 3) consistent sched memory headroom.
[03:32] Marcus: question about secret handling: can we rotate keys without downtime?
[03:36] Priya: yes we have rolling key rotation for service principals and KMS-backed keys, but the private deployment has different SLA; i'll document exact rotation windows.
[03:45] Jordan: good. ok, next i want to talk about the canary timeline — customer asked for 10% traffic cutover for a week then ramp. proposed date 2026-04-14. thoughts?
[03:55] Ethan: 14th works if peering and quant parity are done by 12th.
[04:00] Lena: we also need dashboarding for token-level cost and latency per route — can Redwood share a lightweight dashboard?
[04:06] Jordan: yes our console can give per-route latency and token spend; we can give short-lived dashboard access.
[04:11] Marcus: also need trace context in spans — does your SDK propagate trace IDs?
[04:15] Priya: yes we support trace propagation headers, and we can add a tracing hook for your observability stack.
[04:19] Rita: on the security front, we want a written SLA around fallback behavior if model variants fail; e.g., automatic fallback to smaller model vs blocking traffic.
[04:28] Jordan: we have fallback policies — can configure automatic fallback to lower-cost model or route to another region; i'll include the policy examples.
[04:34] Ethan: what about competitor lock-in? MegaCloud offers a simpler token pricing but no KV cache optimization. we want to understand unit economics for 50M monthly tokens.
[04:43] Jordan: we can run a unit-econ calc — i'll include dedicated vs hosted scenarios; dedicated often wins at high volume but has commit requirements.
[04:50] Marcus: any immediate infra changes we should make?
[04:53] Priya: two quick tweaks: increase scheduler memory headroom to avoid kv evictions, and set batch_size cap to prevent large bursts creating huge batches.
[05:01] Lena: ok we'll implement scheduler change in staging today.
[05:04] Jordan: perfect. action items recap: jordan share security packet + pricing, priya run 4-bit vs 8-bit perf and burst benchmark, carlos and marcus finalize peering cidr and allowlist, rita to send a list of SOC2 questions.
[05:16] Ethan: quick note — our compliance lead also wants to know about data residency (logs in region). we need to confirm logs will stay in us-east-1.
[05:25] Carlos: we can configure log sink region to us-east-1, will make that explicit in the doc.
[05:29] Jordan: ok, i'll add that to the next steps.
[05:33] Marcus: one more infra fallback Q — if you lose a GPU node, is there an automatic fallback to CPU or another region?
[05:40] Priya: automatic fallback is region-based; we don't fall back to CPU for production realtime because performance differs; we route to another compatible node or scaled pool. for critical timeouts we can configure immediate HTTP 503s with retry policy.
[05:54] Lena: that makes sense.
[05:58] Jordan: last, timeline recap — peering and allowlist by 2026-04-08, security Q&A answered by 2026-04-08, bench followups by 2026-04-09, canary on 2026-04-14. any objections?
[06:12] Ethan: no objections.
[06:14] Rita: i'll compile security questions and send to jordan and priya.
[06:18] Jordan: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the sheets and the docs.
[06:22] Carlos: thanks all.
[06:24] (call ends)
